title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization
abstract: arXiv:2608.19746v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Personalized text generation aims to make LLMs write in a specific individual's style, yet existing benchmarks measure task accuracy or preference alignment rather than whether the model's output actually resembles the target author's writing. We introduce PersonalBench, a benchmark that evaluates inference-time personalization methods through three independent lenses: LUAR (a trained authorship verification model), an LLM-as-judge, and automated stylometrics. Across 50 authors, 1,000 generations, and two model families (Qwen 3, GLM-4), we find that personalization methods do produce author-differentiated output (LUAR discriminates target authors within generated text at AUC=0.918) but this differentiation never crosses the human-LLM boundary. All methods achieve LUAR similarity to real authors in the range 0.484-0.508, below the cross-author human floor of 0.626 (ceiling 0.756). The LLM's own authorship fingerprint dominates: generated

translated_title: PersonalBench：衡量LLM个性化中的作者身份差距
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.19746v1 公告类型：新 摘要：个性化文本生成旨在使LLM以特定个体的风格写作，但现有基准衡量的是任务准确性或偏好对齐，而非模型输出是否真正相似于目标作者的写作风格。我们引入了PersonalBench，一个通过三个独立视角评估推理时个性化方法的基准：LUAR（一个训练的作者身份验证模型）、LLM作为评判者，以及自动化文体测量。在50位作者、1000次生成和两个模型家族（Qwen 3、GLM-4）中，我们发现个性化方法确实产生了作者区分的输出（LUAR在生成文本中区分目标作者的AUC=0.918），但这种区分从未跨越人机边界。所有方法对真实作者的LUAR相似度在0.484-0.508范围内，低于跨作者人类下限0.626（上限0.756）。LLM自身的作者身份指纹占主导地位：生成的
tldr: 本文提出PersonalBench基准，发现LLM个性化方法虽能区分不同作者风格，但生成文本与真实人类作者的写作相似度始终低于人类基线，表明存在显著的作者身份差距。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PersonalBench, revealing that LLM personalization methods can differentiate author styles but consistently fall below human authorship similarity baselines, highlighting a significant authorship gap.
